question: Improve the part in capitals: The government has ANNOUNCED ABOUT a new housing scheme.
explanation: 'Announce' is transitive and takes no preposition.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 3)
options: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
Had he worked harder, he will have passed.
If I was you, I will accept the offer.
Were I to had known, I would have stopped.
explanation: Second conditional uses 'were' and 'would'.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: A bolt from the blue.
explanation: It denotes a total surprise.

question: Had the committee _____ the proposal earlier, the delay could have been _____ .
explanation: Third conditional needs past participles.

question: The athlete's _____ rise to fame was followed by an equally _____ fall.
explanation: 'Equally' demands a matching sudden fall.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The reason he failed is BECAUSE he did not prepare adequately.
explanation: 'The reason ... is that' is correct; 'because' is redundant.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 4)
options: The news were received with delight.
The police have arrested the suspect.
explanation: 'Police' is plural; 'news', 'mathematics', 'furniture' are singular.

question: The treaty was signed _____ opposition from hardliners, _____ the moderates hailed it as historic.
explanation: 'Despite' plus 'while' gives the right contrast.

question: Find the part with an error: Between the (A) / three brothers, the property (B) / was divided equally. (C)
explanation: For more than two persons use 'among'.

question: The scheme was launched with great _____ but soon _____ for want of funds.
explanation: Grand launch followed by failure.

question: The minister's statement was _____ by the media as an attempt to _____ public attention from the scam.
explanation: Critics brand it a diversion tactic.

question: The bank has decided to _____ the interest rates, _____ the burden on borrowers.
explanation: Cutting rates eases the burden.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Over the long term, it also raises the risk of heart disease.
Q. Sleep deprivation affects far more than one's mood.
R. Studies link it to weaker memory and slower reaction times.
S. Adults are therefore advised to sleep seven to nine hours each night.
explanation: Statement, short-term effects, long-term effect, advice.

question: The two nations, long _____ rivals, have finally agreed to _____ their differences through dialogue.
explanation: Bitter rivals agreeing to dialogue will resolve differences.

question: He was reluctant to _____ his opinion lest it should _____ his superiors.
explanation: Fear of offending explains reluctance to voice an opinion.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. The model was soon replicated in many developing countries, including India.
Q. Repayment rates turned out to be remarkably high.
R. Microfinance began as a modest experiment in Bangladesh.
S. Small loans were given to poor women without collateral.
explanation: Origin, method, result, replication.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 6)
options: Hardly had she entered than the lights went out.
Hardly she had entered when the lights went out.
Hardly did she entered when the lights went out.
Hardly had she entered when the lights went out.
explanation: 'Hardly had ... when' is the correct pattern.

question: Find the part with an error: Not only the (A) / officers but also the (B) / clerk were present at the meeting. (C)
explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer subject 'clerk', so 'was'.

question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The trust received a MUNIFICENT donation from an alumnus.
explanation: Munificent means very generous; stingy is the opposite.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To rest on one's laurels.
options: To be content with past success and make no further effort
explanation: It means relying on earlier achievements.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To cut corners.
options: To do something cheaply by skipping proper procedure
explanation: It implies neglecting thoroughness to save time or money.

question: _____ the rains were scanty this year, farm output is expected to remain _____ .
explanation: Scanty rains cause weak output.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 1)
options: Each of the clerks has submitted his own form.
He is more taller than any other boy in his class.
Neither of the two proposals were accepted.
The scenery of the hills are breathtaking.
explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb and pronoun.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 14)
options: She said me she would come.
She told me that she would come.
She told that she would come.
She said to that she would come.
explanation: 'Tell' needs an indirect object.

question: Find the part with an error: The two sisters look so alike (A) / that it is difficult (B) / to distinguish one from the another. (C)
explanation: It should be 'one from the other'.

question: Find the part with an error: The government has (A) / lesser funds at its disposal (B) / than it did a decade ago. (C)
explanation: 'Lesser' is wrongly used; 'less' or 'fewer' funds is required.

question: Improve the part in capitals: Unless you DO NOT WORK hard, you will not clear the exam.
explanation: 'Unless' already carries negative meaning.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To blow the whistle.
explanation: It means to reveal illicit activity.

question: Find the part with an error: One should (A) / always keep their (B) / promises. (C)
explanation: The pronoun must agree with 'one': 'one's promises'.

question: He is senior (A) / than me (B) / in the bank. (C)
explanation: 'Senior' takes 'to', not 'than': 'senior to me'.

question: Improve the part in capitals: Having finished the audit, THE REPORT WAS SENT BY THE MANAGER to the head office.
options: the report being sent by the manager
the report had been sent by the manager
explanation: The participial phrase must modify the manager.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. A downgrade, in contrast, makes borrowing costlier.
Q. Credit rating agencies assess the ability of borrowers to repay their debts.
R. That is why governments and companies guard their ratings closely.
S. A high rating lets a borrower raise funds at a lower interest rate.
explanation: Definition, benefit, contrast, conclusion.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The CEO tried to ALLEVIATE the concerns of investors.
explanation: Alleviate means to make less severe.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The manager insisted that every employee SUBMITS the report by Friday.
explanation: Subjunctive after 'insisted that' takes the base form.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 18)
options: Each of the boys has a bicycle.
Each of the boys are having a bicycle.
Each of the boys have a bicycle.
Each of the boy has a bicycle.
explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb.

question: Improve the part in capitals: Each of the players HAVE scored a goal.
explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb: 'has'.

question: _____ the revenue targets were met ahead of schedule, the management decided to _____ the staff with a special bonus.
explanation: Cause and reward are logical.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Others, lacking funds, have had to shut down.
Q. Public libraries were once the primary gateway to knowledge for ordinary citizens.
R. Many libraries have responded by offering free digital access and training.
S. The spread of the internet has changed that role considerably.
explanation: Past role, change, response, and 'others' contrast.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The new scheme is more beneficial THAN ANY scheme launched so far.
explanation: Comparison within the same class needs 'other'.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. The regulator has since tightened supervision of such institutions.
Q. Weak governance then led to poor lending decisions and mounting bad loans.
R. Cooperative banks were set up to extend credit to people excluded from formal finance.
S. Over time, however, many of them were captured by local political interests.
explanation: Purpose, capture, consequence, regulatory response.
